title: 次, 遍: how many times
summary: Lets you say how many times you do something, as in 我去过两次.
structure: Verb + Number + 遍 (from start to end)
explanation:
次 counts how many times an action happens. It goes AFTER the verb: 我去过两次 'I've been twice', 我看了三次 'I watched it three times.' With an object, the number + 次 usually comes before it: 我去过两次中国.

遍 also counts times, but stresses doing the whole thing from start to finish: 请再说一遍 'Please say it once more', 这本书我看了三遍 'I read this book three times (all the way through).'

examples.en: I've seen this film three times.
I go running once a day.

mistakes.why: Number + 次 comes after the verb.
Counting actions uses 次 or 遍, not 个.

exercises.en: I've been to Beijing three times.
why: 个 counts things and people, not actions.

exercises.prompt: Your teacher spoke too fast. You say:
why: 一遍 comes after the verb.
Actions are counted with 遍, not 个.
Correct: verb + 过 + 两次 + object.
两次 must come after the verb.
Use 两, not 二, before a measure word.

exercises.en: Read the text once from start to finish.
why: Correct: 遍 = once through, start to end.
块 is for money or pieces.

exercises.prompt: Which means 'I swim twice a week'?
why: Correct: the number of times goes after the verb.
两次 can't go before everything else.
Actions are counted with 次, not 个.
